To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the own price elasticities of demand for a differentiated product are much larger in magnitude when inventory levels are controlled for.

(1) the demand for a storable product is affected by the current level of inventory, (2) the price response of consumers to a promotion is substantially reduced when we control for inventory, (3) the own-price elasticity is reduced when we control only for inventory, but is not reduced when we control also for consumption shares and consumption price, (4) the cross-price elasticity is reduced substantially when we control only or also for consumption shares.

(a) the long run response of consumption to a temporary promotion of a stora- ble differentiated product is less than the short run response, and (b) controlling for inventory in a differentiated products model reduces the long run response by more than 50 percent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of controlling for temporary promotions in a differentiated product model of consumer demand.
the problem of estimating long-run demand elasticities in a differentiated products model.
the estimation of a differentiated products model of consumer demand for a storable good, and with the estimation of supply.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model does a good job of capturing the dynamics in the market for the good under consideration.
the use of inventory in a differentiated products model is a necessary and useful tool in the estimation of the effects of temporary promotions.
controlling for inventries in a differentiated products model of consumer demand is a necessary step in obtaining accurate estimates of demand and supply elasticities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inclusion of dynamic elements into a differentiated products demand model can help us understand the impact of temporary promotions.
the inclusion of inventories is an important step in the estimation of differentiated products models.

the inclusion of inventories and consumption shares and prices into a static model of consumer demand and supply yields results that are consistent with the structural dynamics literature, and that this is true even when the demand system is not linear in prices and the supply system is not linear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the static demand model is misspecified when the good is storable.

the use of a static demand and price model with inventory as an explanatory variable can produce estimates of demand elasticities and price coefficients that are similar to those obtained using more complicated dynamic models.
it is necessary to control for the effects of inventory when using a static demand model to study the effects of temporary promotions.
